key_facts: The role was Class A Driver. On Sept. 22, 2023, Swift driver recruiters Robin Kaufman and Matt Hutto emailed Plaintiff through Tenstreet about completing a Class A Driver application. On Sept. 25, Tenstreet posted a DriverIQ employment document and an FMCSA Clearinghouse result; FMCSA emailed that SWIFT TRANSPORTATION CO OF ARIZONA LLC (USDOT 54283) had requested Clearinghouse access. On Sept. 26, Swift Recruiting emailed an encrypted pre-adverse letter, later decrypted. On Oct. 5, Swift sent a post-adverse letter stating it had decided not to employ Plaintiff based in whole or in part on consumer reports from Asurint, Tenstreet, DriverIQ, FMCSA-DOT, and Equifax Work Number. The decrypted packet is pleaded as known fact: National Criminal without Sex Offender Clear; federal criminal Clear; completed county criminal Clear; NSOPW remained Processing on every snapshot furnished to Plaintiff; the furnished packet contains neither a completed hit nor a completed no-record, and no California source-of-record line; Clearinghouse Driver Not Prohibited. The file does not contain a written offer, a terminal assignment, or a rate of pay. The § 290 count is information and belief that Swift used preliminary sex-offender-registry information from that in-process NSOPW component, in whole or in part, in the denial. What the completed criminal / MVR / PSP / CDLIS components contain is not information disclosed pursuant to Penal Code § 290.46. Do not treat this packet as proof that Home Depot, Best Buy, or AT&T used the registry.
